When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10**: near-zero crash signal, price calm vs VIX Spike Tier **4/4** EXTREME: **85%** probability, skew active, backwardation active, adaptive active
Price hasn't broken yet but the options market is at maximum hedging intensity. Trust the VIX detector: it measures what investors are paying to hedge against next, not what has already happened. Skew and backwardation firing together reflect near-term protection demand that typically precedes the price move.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime State **8/10** STABLE: no regime shift detected vs Macro Regime TRANSITIONAL: only **25%** confidence
Two systems read the same market and disagree on whether a transition is underway. The regime state sees structural stability; the macro regime model picks up a shift it can't confirm. At **25%** confidence in a transitional read, lean toward reducing exposure rather than adding it.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime reads TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence. The system sees a shift forming but cannot confirm where it is heading.

TRANSITIONAL at low confidence is the most difficult state to size into: the prior regime is losing coherence and the new one hasn't established itself. The regime state reads STABLE at 8/10 with MIXED bias simultaneously, adding internal disagreement between the two systems.

Smaller position sizes and fewer directional commitments are appropriate until the macro regime resolves to a confirmed state or the MIXED bias clears toward one side.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means assets that normally move together have stopped doing so; correlation drift is the shift in that statistical relationship over a recent window. Today's composite is ELEVATED: 51% of 43 tracked pairs are diverging, net bearish bias 18, 20 bearish pairs against 2 bullish, with the Mother Jaws composite at 100 (its maximum).

All six top pairs score DEEP DIVERG at 80: MOVE vs bonds flipped from +0.77 to -0.01 (bond volatility and bonds themselves nearly decoupled), KRE vs XLF from +0.11 to -0.49 (regional banks breaking hard from broader financials), TLT vs SHY from +0.06 to -0.62 (long duration separating from short in a way that rarely stays benign), QQQ vs SPY from +0.43 to -0.16, EEM vs EFA from +0.28 to -0.28, and MTUM vs SPY from +0.40 to -0.18. When this many pairs break their historical relationships simultaneously and in the same bearish direction, correlation structure is repricing.

AI read · the cross-region tape

BTC at +3.9% over five days is the strongest reading across all tracked regions and assets. The bid is in BTC specifically: SOL is down -1.4% over the same period, so capital is rotating within crypto rather than flowing in from outside.

The rest of the picture is broadly negative. KOSPI is the worst performer at -3.6% in Asia while Shanghai holds +0.7%, a split that reflects idiosyncratic Korea-specific pressure rather than a clean Asian growth call.

Europe is uniformly weak: FTSE leads at -1.2% and CAC lags at -2.1%, meaning the European leader is still down on the week. In the US, the Dow edges +0.2% while the Russell drops -1.5%: capital is shifting toward large-cap and away from smaller, rate-sensitive companies, which aligns directly with the KRE vs XLF divergence and the active VIX backwardation signal.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

A Crash Index of 1/10 alongside a VIX Spike Tier of 4/4 EXTREME is a coherent state. The Crash Index measures realized price disruption: drawdowns and breadth damage that already happened.

At 1/10, almost none of those have fired. The VIX Spike Detector measures what the options market is paying to hedge against next: Tier 4 with 85% probability, skew active, backwardation active (near-term implied vol priced above long-term), and the adaptive signal on.

That's the derivatives market pre-positioning for a volatility expansion that hasn't arrived in price yet. These two readings coexist regularly right before a break.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
4 tiers (BROAD / MEDIUM / HIGH / EXTREME) based on the confluence of 3 Validated components: SKEW > 140 (tail-hedge demand), VIX3M/VIX > 1.05 (vol curve inverted), VIX < 16 + ratio > 1.15 (adaptive proxy). Each tier indicates a historical probability of VIX +50% at 60d (cycle backtest 2023-2026, vs baseline 37%). Strict sizing: tier 2 = 1-2% book hedges, tier 3 = 3-5% long-vol, tier 4 = 5-10% MAX (rare confluence).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
